key_insight: At Mach 6, grazing atmospheric particles can excite strong hypersonic boundary-layer instability waves without hitting the surface by crossing the highly receptive critical layer.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for grazing particulates could improve transition-onset predictions for hypersonic vehicles.
method: High-fidelity simulations of grazing and impact–rebound particle trajectories on HIFLIER.
Multiple-scales asymptotic analysis of extended particle–boundary-layer interactions.
Root-mean-square disturbance estimates for submicron grazing particles.
evidence_signal: Particles penetrating less than halfway through the boundary layer produced wavepacket amplitudes comparable to wall-impinging particles, while estimated transition-onset locations were close to flight measurements.
watch_item: Agreement at the studied Mach 6 ascent condition suggests a particulate contribution but does not establish causation or applicability across flight conditions.
paper_title: On the role of grazing atmospheric particles in hypersonic boundary-layer receptivity
